security_audit.summary: All 264 static alerts are false positives involving documented publishing, literal Markdown, validation rules, or local safeguards. A separate directory-packaging race can upload unintended files if a concurrent writer replaces validated paths with symlinks. No evidence found of prompt injection, intentional credential theft, or concealed upload destinations.

remediation.issue: Directory packaging checks file types before zip reopens paths, allowing concurrent replacement with symlinks.
remediation.suggestion: Copy files into a private snapshot using descriptor-relative traversal, O_NOFOLLOW, and regular-file checks; package only that snapshot and verify its contents.

semantic_findings.title: Directory Packaging Can Follow Replaced Symlinks
semantic_findings.description: Collection rejects symlinks using lstat, but zip later reopens the selected paths without a stable snapshot. A concurrent writer can replace a selected file or ancestor with a symlink to readable files outside the directory. Archive verification compares names, not source identity, so an unchanged innocuous filename can pass inspection and upload unintended data.

content.user_title: Publish Files and Static Sites to Brewpage
content.value_statement: Sharing local content requires a hosted address and clear access settings. This skill publishes selected content to brewpage.app and returns its link after explicit choices.
actual_capabilities: Publish text and Markdown as rendered pages, JSON as documents, and individual files through dedicated API endpoints.
Package built static directories into ZIP archives and inspect supplied ZIP archives before uploading.
Filter directory assets by filename and extension, skipping symlinks and hidden entries except the root .well-known directory.
Request explicit namespace and password choices, with optional passwords read from existing local files.
Save owner tokens in mode-600 local history and enforce Git exclusion inside repositories.
Support requested retention, site entry selection, delivery mode, and digest-bound confirmation for flagged archives.
limitations: Requires POSIX tooling; sites also need Node.js and unzip, with zip required for directory packaging.
Hosts static output, not server applications; service limits and publication expiration still apply.
Unlisted links do not enforce access control without passwords, and file contents are not scanned for embedded secrets.
Directory packaging is not race-safe against concurrent source changes; use a trusted, unchanged build directory.

best_practices: Publish trusted, unchanged build output and review file contents for embedded secrets before upload.
Choose namespace, password protection, and retention explicitly; unlisted links alone do not restrict readers.
Review flagged manifests and exact digests, and keep owner-token history private and excluded from version control.
anti_patterns: Publishing source trees or actively changing directories instead of reviewed static build output.
Treating private namespaces as authentication or publishing confidential data without appropriate access protection.
Pasting passwords into chat, exposing owner tokens, or approving an archive digest without reviewing its manifest.

faq.question: What content can I publish?
faq.answer: Text, Markdown, JSON, individual files, built static directories, and inspected ZIP site archives are supported.

faq.question: Does publishing require an account?
faq.answer: No account is required for the documented publishing workflow. Optional account features depend on brewpage.app.

faq.question: Are private namespaces access-controlled?
faq.answer: No. They are unlisted, but anyone with the link can open them unless password protection is enabled.

faq.question: How are passwords and owner tokens handled?
faq.answer: Passwords come from existing local files. Owner tokens stay in protected local history and must not appear in chat.

faq.question: Can this run on native Windows?
faq.answer: Native Windows Python is unsupported. Use Linux, macOS, or WSL with the documented command-line dependencies.

faq.question: How long do publications remain available?
faq.answer: The default requested lifetime is 15 days. Server limits and returned expiration timestamps determine actual retention, including existing deduplicated publications.
